title: The unramified lci finite-Hilbert locus is open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of stacks in groupoids on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and object descent is effective. Suppose $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}h_T$ is an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. Assume each $X_y\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every integer $d\geq1$, the fibred groupoids $\mathcal H_d(F)$ and $\mathcal L_d(F)$ [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids] are fppf stacks, and the inclusion $j_d:\mathcal L_d(F)\to\mathcal H_d(F)$ is representable by schemes and an open immersion: for every scheme $T$ and $\xi\in\mathcal H_d(F)(T)$, $h_T\times_{\mathcal H_d(F)}\mathcal L_d(F)$ is naturally represented by an open subscheme $T^\circ\subseteq T$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Equivalently, for every scheme map $T'\to T$, $\xi|_{T'}$ lies in $\mathcal L_d(F)$ if and only if $T'\to T$ factors through $T^\circ$. Neither surjectivity of $F$ nor algebraicity of either $\mathcal X$ or $\mathcal Y$ is required.

proof.text: Fix $d\geq1$. For an fppf descent datum of Hilbert objects as in [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids], first descend the finite degree-$d$ covers $Z_i\to T_i$ and their isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-fppf-descent], obtaining $Z\to T$. Identify $Z_i=Z\times_TT_i$; these form an fppf covering of $Z$ by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. The overlap arrows induce descent data for $y_i$ on $T_i$ and $x_i$ on $Z_i$. Effectivity for the assumed stacks $\mathcal Y$ and $\mathcal X$ gives $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ and $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$. The compatibility square defining a Hilbert arrow says exactly that the transported $\alpha_i$ agree on overlaps. The isomorphism sheaf in $\mathcal Y$ glues them to $\alpha:y|_Z\simeq F(x)$. This gives the descended object. For arrows, descend the cover isomorphism uniquely by the same finite-cover lemma, then descend $b$ and $a$ by the isomorphism sheaves of $\mathcal Y$ and $\mathcal X$. The compatibility square holds because it holds on the covering. Thus $\mathcal H_d(F)$ is an fppf stack.

source.place: Tag 05WB (lemma-hilbert-d-stack), proof, including the omitted arrow-gluing check.

proof.text: For $\xi=(Z\to T,y,x,\alpha)$ write $u:Z\to X_y$ using the explicit represented $2$-fibre product in [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. Given $g:T^\prime\to T$, identify $X_{g^*y}$ with $T^\prime\times_TX_y$. On a test scheme $V$, both classify a map $t:V\to T^\prime$, an object $a\in\mathcal X(V)$ and an isomorphism $(gt)^*y\simeq F(a)$, with exactly the same compatible arrows. The resulting bijections of represented sheaves are natural in $V$, so they and their inverse are inverse maps of spaces, whose maps are natural transformations. Fibre products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The pulled-back pair is $(x|_{Z\times_TT^\prime},\alpha|_{Z\times_TT^\prime})$, so its associated map is exactly $u_{T^\prime}:Z\times_TT^\prime\to X_y\times_TT^\prime$. For an isomorphism of Hilbert objects, the defining equation $F(a)\alpha=(h^*\alpha^\prime)(b|_Z)$ identifies these pairs and their maps. Thus the conditions concern this pulled-back map and do not depend on representatives.

proof.text: The morphism $p:Z\to T$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. It is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. It is also locally of finite type: on affine charts a finitely presented algebra is a quotient of a polynomial algebra in finitely many variables, whose coordinate images generate it. The other projection $q:X_y\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by hypothesis. Here the space-map properties have the chart meaning fixed by [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]: there exist surjective etale scheme charts $V\to B$ and $U\to A\times_BV$ with $U\to V$ having the specified scheme property. This is the interpretation of flatness and local finite presentation in the hypotheses, and of unramifiedness and lci in the two parameter-open statements. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-source-unramified-base-open] and [lem-sfb-space-relative-lci-parameter-open] to the triangle $Z\xrightarrow{u}X_y\to T$. They give open subschemes $W_{\mathrm{ur}},W_{\mathrm{lci}}\subseteq T$. Set $T^\circ=W_{\mathrm{ur}}\cap W_{\mathrm{lci}}$. A morphism $g:T^\prime\to T$ factors through this intersection exactly when it factors through both opens. The two universal properties and step 2 give precisely $\xi|_{T^\prime}\in\mathcal L_d(F)$. Taking $T^\prime=T^\circ$ and then any map into it also proves stability of the subcategory under every pullback.

Over $g:T^\prime\to T$, the 2-fibre product $h_T\times_{\mathcal H_d(F)}\mathcal L_d(F)$ has objects an $\eta\in\mathcal L_d(F)(T^\prime)$ together with an isomorphism $\xi|_{T^\prime}\simeq\eta$. Since $\mathcal L_d(F)$ is a full subcategory, this groupoid is empty unless $\xi|_{T^\prime}$ belongs to it, and otherwise is contractible: between two such pairs there is exactly one arrow, obtained by composing their displayed isomorphisms. By step 3 it is therefore naturally equivalent to $h_{T^\circ}(T^\prime)$. These equivalences respect restriction, so the 2-fibre product is represented by $T^\circ$. Its projection to $h_T$ is the inclusion of this open subscheme, an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion]. This proves the asserted scheme representability and the universal factorization clause.

source.place: Tag 06CL (lemma-lci-locus-stack-in-groupoids), identification of the scheme pullback.

proof.text: It remains to check descent for $\mathcal L_d(F)$. Its arrow sheaves are the arrow sheaves of $\mathcal H_d(F)$ by fullness. A descent datum in $\mathcal L_d(F)$ descends in $\mathcal H_d(F)$ by step 1 to some $\xi$ over $T$. Each cover map $T_i\to T$ factors through the open $T^\circ$ for $\xi$ by steps 2--3. Since the family is jointly surjective, $|T^\circ|=|T|$; the open subscheme is therefore $T$ itself. Consequently $\xi$ lies in $\mathcal L_d(F)$. Uniqueness and the given overlap isomorphisms are inherited from the full subcategory. This proves that $\mathcal L_d(F)$ is an fppf stack. The argument has used only the scheme tests of $F$ and the stated stack axioms, so requires neither surjectivity nor algebraicity of $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$.

source.place: Tag 06CL (lemma-lci-locus-stack-in-groupoids), final descent assertion, proved directly rather than assuming the stacks are algebraic.
